Learn how our infrastructure works and suggest improvements

Exposure to, or a strong interest in, Infrastructure-as-Code tools (for example, Terraform or similar) and version control such as Git
A basic understanding of CI/CD pipelines that enable automated, reliable delivery of infrastructure changes
Awareness of monitoring and observability concepts, including metrics, logging, and alerting
Basic scripting ability in a language such as Python, Bash, or PowerShell to automate operational tasks and workflows
Certifications such as AWS Cloud Practitioner are a plus
Exposure to Microsoft 365 services such as Entra ID, Intune, Defender, and Conditional Access
Experience with Oracle RDBMS, Oracle middleware, or PostgreSQL
Some experience using Linux and Windows, including the command line; exposure to Ansible is a bonus
Familiarity to containers (for example, Docker or ECS, our current platform) or Kubernetes/EKS

descriptionText:
LDMS is hiring a Junior Infrastructure Engineer to help build and support the cloud infrastructure behind its SaaS products and internal tools. The role also supports Oracle databases and middleware and end-user computing, while contributing to infrastructure improvements, proof-of-concept solutions, and documentation.
Responsibilities
Help build and support the cloud infrastructure that underpins our SaaS products and internal tooling – this will be your primary focus
Support our Oracle RDBMS and middleware and our end user computing estate – for example, database patching and backups, user requests, and device management through Intune – learning these technologies and helping the wider team support them (no prior experience needed)
Plan, implement and test solutions with growing independence, knowing when to ask for help
Learn how our infrastructure works and suggest improvements
Help build proof-of-concept solutions to evaluate new technologies
Write clear documentation so others can understand and build on your work
Learn from experienced engineers, who will mentor you on technology, architecture and best practices
Skills
A proactive, self-starting attitude and a willingness to ask questions
Curiosity and an appetite for exploring new technologies
A genuine enjoyment of learning from others and sharing what you learn
A belief that constant improvement underpins good engineering
1–2 years' experience in an infrastructure, cloud, or IT operations role, or a relevant degree plus around a year of industry experience (for example, a placement year or internship)
An understanding of how cloud infrastructure supports production services
Some hands-on experience with core AWS services such as EC2, VPC, ECS, RDS, and IAM, alongside a basic understanding of cloud security and networking fundamentals (for example, VPCs, subnets, and firewall rules)
Exposure to, or a strong interest in, Infrastructure-as-Code tools (for example, Terraform or similar) and version control such as Git
A basic understanding of CI/CD pipelines that enable automated, reliable delivery of infrastructure changes
Awareness of monitoring and observability concepts, including metrics, logging, and alerting
Basic scripting ability in a language such as Python, Bash, or PowerShell to automate operational tasks and workflows
Certifications such as AWS Cloud Practitioner are a plus
Exposure to Microsoft 365 services such as Entra ID, Intune, Defender, and Conditional Access
Experience with Oracle RDBMS, Oracle middleware, or PostgreSQL
Some experience using Linux and Windows, including the command line; exposure to Ansible is a bonus
Familiarity to containers (for example, Docker or ECS, our current platform) or Kubernetes/EKS
Benefits
Hybrid/Flexible Working
Mentorship from experienced engineers on technology, architecture and best practices
Company Overview
LDMS are pioneers of Credit Software, with a long history of delivering state-of-the-art loan management solutions across EMEA. It was founded in 2011, and is headquartered in Cardiff, Cardiff, GBR, with a workforce of 51-200 employees. Its website is https://www.ldms.com/.
